봉영여중 추가지문 - 3학년
주제찾기
1 9번 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
Some shoppers lose their desire for an item the moment everyone else seems to have it. This reaction is known as the snob effect. People affected by it value goods mainly because few others can get them. Picture a brand that sells just 500 pairs of special sneakers. Fans rush to buy them since they are so hard to find. But when the brand later makes millions of pairs, many of those fans walk away. Owning the shoes no longer makes them feel different from others. For this reason, companies often keep their products limited to make them look rare and special.
①why mass production always lowers the quality of sneakers
②how a product’s rarity affects some consumers’ desire to buy it
③the reasons people follow their friends’ shopping choices
④ways to save money when buying limited-edition goods
⑤the history of famous sneaker brands and their designs
2 10번 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
Normally, people buy less of a product when its price goes up. With Veblen goods, however, the opposite can happen. These are items such as luxury watches, sports cars, and designer handbags. Buyers choose them not only for their quality but also to show off their wealth and status. Economist Thorstein Veblen called this kind of spending conspicuous consumption. A high price makes such goods look more prestigious. So when a luxury brand raises the price of a handbag, even more people may want it. In short, the price itself becomes a symbol of success.
①why luxury goods are usually made with better materials
②how people can avoid spending too much money on watches
③why demand for some goods rises as their prices go up
④the life and works of the economist Thorstein Veblen
⑤how companies lower prices to attract more customers

봉영여중 추가지문 - 3학년
주제찾기
3 11번 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
Romeo and Juliet knew each other for only five days, yet they fell deeply in love. One psychologist thinks the problems they faced made their love stronger. Because their parents tried to keep them apart, they wanted each other even more. Interestingly, the same feeling appears when we go shopping. We tend to want something more when we think we might lose the chance to have it. Sellers use this by saying things like “Only three days left!” Worried about missing out, buyers often purchase the item immediately. So when you see a limited-time sale, it is wise to ask whether you truly need the item.
①how parents can help their children make good friends
②why Romeo and Juliet’s story has stayed popular for centuries
③the reasons sellers offer large discounts on old products
④how fear of losing something makes people want it more
⑤the best ways to plan a shopping budget

봉영여중 추가지문 - 3학년
요지찾기
4 9번 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
Most of us like things that are popular, but some people feel the opposite way. They want a product most when it is rare or hard to get. If only a few hundred pairs of sneakers are sold, these buyers are eager to own a pair. Once the same sneakers are produced in huge numbers, however, the shoes lose their appeal. This is the snob effect, and it works in the opposite direction from the bandwagon effect. While bandwagon buyers want what everyone has, snob buyers want what makes them different. Knowing this, companies release limited-edition and luxury goods to create a feeling of rarity. Buyers who value being unique are often ready to pay more for such goods.
①유행하는 제품을 사야 사회에서 인정받을 수 있다.
②한정판 제품은 품질이 좋아서 비싸게 팔린다.
③기업은 제품을 대량 생산해야 더 많은 이익을 얻는다.
④어떤 소비자들은 제품이 희소할수록 더 가치 있게 여기고, 흔해지면 관심을 잃는다.
⑤소비자는 친구들이 산 물건을 따라 사는 경향이 있다.
5 10번 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
Most products sell less when they become more expensive. Veblen goods are different, because their demand may grow as their prices climb. People buy luxury brands, expensive watches, or sports cars partly to display their wealth and social position. Thorstein Veblen, an American economist, described this as conspicuous consumption. For example, a shopper may pick a costly watch over a cheaper one simply because the price makes it seem prestigious. Likewise, when a brand raises the price of a handbag, it can look even more exclusive and sell better. In these cases, a high price is not a reason to stop buying. Instead, it is the very reason people want the product.
①어떤 제품은 비쌀수록 부와 지위의 상징이 되어 수요가 늘어난다.
②명품은 품질이 뛰어나기 때문에 가격이 비싸다.
③소비자는 가격이 오르면 대체로 구매를 줄인다.
④과시적 소비는 경제 성장에 도움이 된다.
⑤합리적인 소비자는 가격보다 품질을 중시한다.

10 9번 밑줄 친 부분이 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
A sneaker company decides to make only 500 pairs of a new design. Because the shoes are so hard to get, many people line up to buy them. Months later, the company produces millions of the same pair. Suddenly, some of the first buyers stop wearing them. Their shoes have become just another pair in the crowd. This is a typical example of the snob effect. People who are influenced by it value products that are rare or exclusive. When too many others own the same item, it loses its charm for them.
①a pair that is too small for most people to wear
②a pair that was made with cheaper materials
③a pair that no longer makes its owner stand out
④a pair that is sold at a much higher price

11 10번 밑줄 친 부분이 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
Imagine two watches that keep time equally well. One costs $100, and the other costs $10,000. Surprisingly, some customers choose the expensive one without hesitation. For them, the price tag is part of what they are buying. A high price makes the watch seem more prestigious. Wearing it tells others that its owner is wealthy and successful. This is called the Veblen effect. It explains why demand for some luxury goods rises along with their prices.

②They believe expensive watches keep better time.
③They plan to sell the watch later for a profit.
④They value the high price because it shows their wealth.

서술형 (본문 제시) · 9번
Why do some people stop wanting a product after it becomes popular? This behavior is called the snob effect. The snob effect refers to people’s tendency to value a product because it is rare or exclusive. As more people buy the same product, it becomes less attractive to those consumers. For example, imagine that a company releases only 500 pairs of limited-edition sneakers. Many people want to buy them because they are difficult to obtain. However, if the company later produces millions of the same sneakers, some buyers lose interest. They no longer feel special because many other people own the same shoes. The snob effect is the opposite of the bandwagon effect. The bandwagon effect occurs when people buy a product simply because many others are buying it. In contrast, the snob effect encourages people to choose products that help them stand out from the crowd. Companies often use the snob effect in their marketing strategies. They release limited-edition products or luxury products to create a sense of rarity and exclusivity. As a result, consumers who value uniqueness may be willing to pay higher prices for these products. Researchers have found that scarcity can increase or decrease demand depending on whether consumers are seeking exclusivity or popularity.

서술형 (본문 제시) · 10번
The Veblen effect is a type of consumer behavior in which people are more willing to buy a product because it is expensive. Unlike most products, demand for Veblen goods may increase as their prices rise. Consumers often purchase these products to show their wealth, success, or social status. Luxury brands, expensive watches, sports cars, and designer handbags are common examples of Veblen goods. This idea is based on the concept of conspicuous consumption, introduced by the American economist Thorstein Veblen. According to this theory, some people buy expensive goods not only for their quality but also to display their financial success. A customer chooses a luxury watch instead of a cheaper one because its high price makes the watch seem more prestigious. A luxury brand raises the price of a handbag, and demand increases because the product appears even more exclusive. The Veblen effect is the tendency for demand to rise as the price of a product rises because the product symbolizes wealth, prestige, or social status.
